scenario: [RARC.7.15], [RARC.5.6.3]: a clock move retracts nothing; an expired fact stays in working memory until the next pump. On the mock clock, a `Pulse` (`scope ttl 50_ms`) is asserted at 1 s and the clock advanced by 100 ms, past its deadline at 1.05 s, and nothing pumps. `temporal_sequence` reads working memory after the last step ([RCTS.1.2.31]), which here is the advance, so the expired `Pulse` is still there: `fact_count_after: 1`. What it discriminates: a runtime that sweeps expired facts when the clock moves counts 0. RTIM.3b's steps end with a pump, so it cannot see this. PATHS: libds's `ds_engine_clock_advance` (clock.c), which moves the mock clock and sweeps nothing; the Mercury runtime's `ds.engine.advance`, which does not call `sweep_expired`.
